Normal because the bars are balanced.
Bimodal because there are two equal peaks.
options.misconception: misreads flat top as two peaks

options.text: Skewed because no peak is visible.
options.misconception: confuses absence of peak with skew

questions.explanation: Roughly equal bar heights indicate a uniform distribution. Flatness differs from bell shape or bimodality.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the most robust spread measure
questions.stem: Which spread measure is least affected by a single extreme outlier?

options.text: Range because it uses only extremes.
Standard deviation because it averages squared deviations.
IQR because it uses middle 50 percent.
Variance because it is squared.

questions.explanation: IQR uses the middle 50 percent, so extremes do not affect it. Range and standard deviation are sensitive to outliers.

questions.stem: If a distribution has a long tail on the left, it is described as what?

options.text: Right-skewed because skew names the peak side.
options.misconception: confuses tail side with peak side

options.text: Uniform because the tail is spread.

Left-skewed because the tail points left.

questions.explanation: Skewness is named by the tail direction. A long left tail means left skew, regardless of peak location.
